title: An Introduction to the Study of the Kabalah
author: W. Wynn Westcott
query: Introduction to the Study of the Kabalah Westcott
epithet: The Golden Dawn founder's primer of the Kabbalah
summary: Westcott's short introduction to the doctrines of the Kabbalah for the English student — the compact primer that shaped how the Golden Dawn and its heirs understood the Tree of Life.

title: The Secret Doctrine in Israel
author: A. E. Waite
query: The Secret Doctrine in Israel Waite Zohar
epithet: Waite's study of the Zohar
summary: Waite's study and paraphrase of the Zohar and its doctrine — the first of his two large books on the Kabbalah, reading it as a monument of Christian-tending mysticism.

title: Jewish Mysticism
author: Joshua Abelson
query: Jewish Mysticism Abelson
epithet: An early English introduction to the tradition
summary: Abelson's short, sympathetic survey of Jewish mysticism from the Merkabah to the Kabbalah — one of the first accessible English accounts, written before Scholem reshaped the field.

title: The Immanence of God in Rabbinical Literature
author: Joshua Abelson
query: Immanence of God in Rabbinical Literature Abelson
epithet: The Shekhinah and the indwelling God
summary: Abelson's study of the rabbinic ideas of the Shekhinah, the Holy Spirit and the divine presence — the background in which the Kabbalah's doctrine of the immanent God took shape.

title: Sefer ha-Zohar (Mantua edition)
author: attributed to Shimon bar Yochai
query: Sefer ha-Zohar Mantua Zohar
epithet: The Book of Splendour in its first printing
summary: The Zohar, the central book of the Kabbalah, in the Mantua editio princeps — the mystical commentary on the Torah whose Aramaic pages became the scripture of Jewish mysticism.

title: Tikkunei ha-Zohar
author: attributed to Shimon bar Yochai
query: Tikkunei ha-Zohar Tikkune Zohar
epithet: Seventy meditations on the first word of the Torah
summary: The 'Emendations of the Zohar', seventy discourses expounding the first word of Genesis — a distinct and enormously influential stratum of the Zoharic literature, printed at Mantua.

title: Pardes Rimonim
author: Moses Cordovero
query: Pardes Rimonim Cordovero
epithet: The Orchard of Pomegranates: Kabbalah systematised
summary: Cordovero's great systematic exposition of the Kabbalah before Luria — thirteen 'gates' ordering the whole doctrine of the sefirot — printed in Kraków and foundational for all later study.

title: Or Ne'erav
author: Moses Cordovero
query: Or Neerav Cordovero
epithet: A defence of and gateway to the study of Kabbalah
summary: Cordovero's short apologia for the study of the Kabbalah and abridged introduction to his own system — the accessible doorway to the vast Pardes Rimonim.

title: Reshit Chochmah
author: Elijah de Vidas
query: Reshit Chokhmah de Vidas
epithet: The Beginning of Wisdom: Kabbalistic ethics
summary: De Vidas's vast manual of moral and devotional life drawn from the Zohar and the school of Safed — the book that carried Cordoverian Kabbalah into everyday Jewish piety.

title: Avodat ha-Kodesh
author: Meir ibn Gabbai
query: Avodat ha-Kodesh ibn Gabbai
epithet: The Service of Holiness, a summa before Luria
summary: Ibn Gabbai's systematic theology of the Kabbalah — on the divine unity, the commandments and prayer — regarded as one of the most coherent statements of the doctrine before the Lurianic turn.

title: Emek ha-Melech
author: Naftali Bacharach
query: Emek ha-Melekh Bacharach
epithet: The Valley of the King: Lurianic Kabbalah diffused
summary: Bacharach's influential and controversial presentation of the Lurianic system — the tzimtzum, the breaking of the vessels and the tikkun — one of the channels by which Luria's Kabbalah spread through Europe.

title: Derech Hashem (The Way of God)
author: Moshe Chaim Luzzatto
query: Derech Hashem Luzzatto Way of God
epithet: The Ramchal's ordered theology of providence
summary: Luzzatto's lucid systematic account of God, providence, the soul and the purpose of creation — the most accessible statement of the Lurianic worldview by the great Ramchal.

title: Kalach Pitchei Chochmah (138 Openings of Wisdom)
author: Moshe Chaim Luzzatto
query: Kalach Pitchei Chokhmah Luzzatto 138
epithet: A hundred and thirty-eight gates to Lurianic wisdom
summary: Luzzatto's systematic key to the Lurianic Kabbalah in one hundred and thirty-eight numbered 'openings' — his attempt to render Isaac Luria's system rationally intelligible.

title: Ma'arekhet ha-Elohut
author: anonymous
query: Maarekhet ha-Elohut Sefer
epithet: The Order of God: an early systematic Kabbalah
summary: One of the earliest systematic treatises of the Kabbalah, laying out the ten sefirot as an ordered structure of divinity — printed with commentaries at Mantua and Ferrara and long a standard text.

title: Chesed le-Avraham
author: Abraham Azulai
query: Chesed le-Avraham Azulai
epithet: A Safed sage's springs of Lurianic wisdom
summary: Azulai's popular compendium of Kabbalistic teaching organised as 'springs' and 'rivers' — a widely read gateway to the doctrines of Cordovero and Luria from the sage of Hebron.

title: Sha'arei Kedushah (The Gates of Holiness)
author: Hayyim Vital
query: Shaarei Kedushah Vital Gates of Holiness
epithet: Luria's disciple on the path to the holy spirit
summary: Vital's manual of ethical and meditative preparation for prophecy and the holy spirit — the practical, attainable face of the Lurianic Kabbalah he did most to record.

title: Shenei Luchot ha-Berit
author: Isaiah Horowitz
query: Shenei Luchot ha-Berit Horowitz Shelah
epithet: The Shelah: law and Kabbalah interwoven
summary: Horowitz's encyclopaedic work — known by its initials, the Shelah — weaving law, ethics and Lurianic mysticism into a guide for the whole of Jewish life, hugely influential in later piety.

title: Sefer Raziel ha-Malakh
author: anonymous
query: Sefer Raziel ha-Malakh Amsterdam
epithet: The Book of the Angel Raziel: practical Kabbalah
summary: The composite grimoire of practical Kabbalah — angelic names, amulets and cosmology said to have been given to Adam by the angel Raziel — in the much-copied Amsterdam printing kept as a house-amulet.

title: Imrei Shefer
author: Abraham Abulafia
query: Imrei Shefer Abulafia
epithet: The ecstatic Kabbalist on letters and prophecy
summary: One of Abulafia's manuals of 'prophetic Kabbalah' — the meditative permutation of the Hebrew letters and divine names as a technique for reaching prophecy — from the founder of the ecstatic school.

title: Zohar Hadash
author: attributed to Shimon bar Yochai
query: Zohar Hadash Cracow
epithet: The 'New Zohar' gathered from the leftover leaves
summary: The Zohar Hadash, the Zoharic material assembled from manuscripts not included in the Mantua and Cremona printings — a further stratum of the great mystical midrash on the Torah.

title: The Traditions of the Jews (Rabbinical Literature)
author: Johann Peter Stehelin
query: Traditions of the Jews Rabbinical Literature Stehelin
epithet: An eighteenth-century English window on Kabbalistic lore
summary: Stehelin's English digest of rabbinic and Kabbalistic traditions — angels, the sefirot, gematria and the world to come — a curiosity through which Georgian readers glimpsed the Kabbalah.

title: The History of the Jews
author: Jacques Basnage
query: History of the Jews Basnage
epithet: The first modern history, with a book on the Kabbalah
summary: Basnage's pioneering history of the Jews since the Dispersion, whose long treatment of the Kabbalah and its sects was for decades the main source through which Christian Europe knew the tradition.

title: Cabala Hebraeorum (from Oedipus Aegyptiacus)
author: Athanasius Kircher
query: Kircher Cabala Hebraeorum Oedipus Aegyptiacus
epithet: Kircher's diagram of the seventy-two names and the Tree
summary: Kircher's treatise on the Hebrew Kabbalah within the Oedipus Aegyptiacus — his great engraved Tree of the sefirot and the seventy-two names, the Baroque Jesuit's reading of Jewish mysticism.

title: Absconditorum a constitutione mundi clavis
author: Guillaume Postel
query: Absconditorum clavis Postel
epithet: Postel's key to the things hidden since the world's foundation
summary: Postel's Kabbalistic 'key to things hidden since the foundation of the world' — the visionary Orientalist's attempt to found a universal restitution on the Zohar, which he was the first Christian to translate.

title: Qabbalah: The Philosophical Writings of Solomon ben Yehudah ibn Gebirol
author: Isaac Myer
query: Qabbalah Isaac Myer ibn Gebirol
epithet: An American Kabbalist on the Fountain of Life
summary: Myer's large illustrated study of the Kabbalah through the philosophy of Solomon ibn Gabirol, with diagrams of the sefirot and the four worlds — an eccentric but richly documented Victorian synthesis.

title: The Kabbalah Unveiled (1926 edition)
author: S. L. MacGregor Mathers
query: Kabbalah Unveiled Mathers Rosenroth
epithet: Rosenroth's Zoharic texts, Englished for the Golden Dawn
summary: Mathers's translation of the principal Zoharic texts from Knorr von Rosenroth's Latin — the Greater and Lesser Holy Assembly and the Book of Concealment — the English Kabbalah of the Golden Dawn.

title: Etz Chaim (Koretz edition)
author: Hayyim Vital
query: Etz Chaim Vital Koretz
epithet: The Tree of Life: Luria's system as recorded by Vital
summary: Vital's record of Isaac Luria's teaching — the tzimtzum, the worlds, the partzufim and the tikkun — the fundamental text of Lurianic Kabbalah, in its early Koretz printing.

title: Tomer Devorah
author: Moses Cordovero
query: Tomer Devorah Cordovero Palm Deborah
epithet: The Palm Tree of Deborah: imitating the sefirot
summary: Cordovero's short ethical classic teaching the imitation of the divine qualities of the sefirot — the little book that turned the abstract theology of the Kabbalah into a practical ethics of character.

title: Ayelet Ahavim
author: Solomon Alkabetz
query: Ayelet Ahavim Alkabetz Song of Songs

author: Moses Cordovero
query: Shiur Komah Cordovero

author: Eleazar of Worms
query: Sefer ha-Rokeach Eleazar of Worms

author: Isidor Kalisch

author: A. E. Waite

author: Adolphe Franck

author: Nurho de Manhar

author: Arthur Edward Waite

author: William Stirling

author: Frederick Bligh Bond and Thomas Simcox Lea

summary: Sepharial's handbook of talismans, magic squares and the Kabbalistic names and seals used to make them — a practical companion to the number-magic of the tradition.

title: Q.B.L., or the Bride's Reception
author: Frater Achad
query: Q.B.L. Bride's Reception Frater Achad

author: Frater Achad
query: Anatomy of the Body of God Frater Achad

author: Éliphas Lévi
query: Magical Ritual of the Sanctum Regnum Levi Westcott

author: P. D. Ouspensky
query: The Symbolism of the Tarot Ouspensky

author: L. W. de Laurence
query: Great Book of Magical Art de Laurence

summary: De Laurence's enormous compendium of ceremonial magic, drawing heavily on the Key of Solomon and the Kabbalistic system of divine names, seals and planetary hours.

title: The Art of Drawing Spirits into Crystals

author: L. W. de Laurence

summary: De Laurence's edition of the key to the tarot, correlating the trumps with the twenty-two Hebrew letters and the paths of the Kabbalistic Tree.

author: Thomas Inman

query: Numbers Their Occult Power and Mystic Virtues Westcott

author: S. L. MacGregor Mathers
query: Kabbalah Unveiled Mathers 1912 Rosenroth

summary: Mathers's English rendering, from Knorr von Rosenroth's Latin, of the Book of Concealed Mystery and the Greater and Lesser Holy Assembly — the Kabbalah the Golden Dawn actually used.

author: Frater Achad

epithet: A restored order of the Tarot on the Tree
summary: Achad's argument for a restored attribution of the tarot trumps to the paths of the Tree of Life — a much-debated intervention in the Hermetic Qabalah of the Golden Dawn tradition.

title: Berashith: An Essay in Ontology
author: Aleister Crowley
query: Berashith Essay in Ontology Crowley
epithet: A Qabalistic meditation on the Nothing
summary: Crowley's early essay reading the first word of Genesis through the Qabalistic doctrine of the negative veils — nothingness, the point and the emergence of the worlds.

title: Egyptian Magic

summary: Farr's short study of Egyptian magic and the science of the divine names and words of power — one of the 'Collectanea Hermetica' produced for the Golden Dawn.

author: W. Wynn Westcott
